sections.heading: Between roles, I kept
sections.intro: Since leaving Fragmatic Technologies in September 2026, I’ve spent the time on hackathons, open source and learning: AI apps built against deadlines, open models running on laptops and phones, and backend systems hardened under failure. I’m looking for my next backend or AI engineering role.

points: Since September I’ve entered five hackathons and challenges, and Perforvisor won Best Use of Tiger Data in DEV’s Hacktoberfest Challenge 2.
I built tools for my own job search too. Huntboard ranks openings against my real experience and never invents a line on my résumé.
I went back to the systems I care about: a hardened rewrite of my job scheduler and fixes merged into open-source projects.

sections.label: SELECTED BUILDS
sections.heading: Hackathon apps, knowledge graphs and local AI.

items.title: Perforvisor won Best Use of Tiger Data.
items.description: Built for DEV’s Hacktoberfest Challenge 2. An AI advisor on open-weight models that reads public reviews (Google Maps via SerpApi), builds a knowledge graph and answers business owners and consumers with cited evidence. Hybrid retrieval and review trends run on Tiger Data Postgres with pgvector and TimescaleDB. The live demo is offline for now: I stopped the GCP GPU that served the models because of hosting cost.

items.title: A medication checker that shows its path.
items.description: Built for Graph Hacks on FalkorDB. A safety agent walks the graph from patient to medicines, ingredients, drug classes, allergies and prescribers to flag conflicts for caregivers, shows the path behind every warning and names who to call. A caregiver assistant hands it questions, and clinician decisions are stored in the graph so both agents remember them next session.

items.title: Two AI apps that never leave your device.
items.description: EchoNote turns a spoken thought into a task, reminder, idea or note with whisper.cpp and Gemma 4 on llama.cpp, fully offline, packaged as RPM, DEB and AppImage. Creative Detour is an Android app that finds free moments in your day and nudges you off your phone, with Gemma 4 writing each nudge on the device through LiteRT-LM.

sections.label: BACK TO THE LAB
sections.heading: The job scheduler, hardened.
sections.lead: I came back to the scheduler I started in January and fixed what broke under failure.
sections.description: It runs immediate, delayed and cron jobs across any number of workers with at-least-once delivery. PostgreSQL is the source of truth, with a transactional outbox feeding Redis Streams. Workers hold leases with heartbeats and fencing tokens, crashed jobs are reclaimed, and failures back off with jitter into a dead letter queue. It ships with priority lanes, rate limiting, backpressure, Prometheus metrics and a Grafana dashboard.

items.title: PostPilot
items.description: A multi-agent Telegram bot that drafts daily posts per platform. A strategist, writer and critic loop over a Postgres-backed queue with RAG over each user's notes, checkpointed runs and shared daily quotas so it runs free.

items.title: Huntboard
items.description: A local-first desktop app for job searching. It collects openings from job boards, deduplicates and ranks them against your real experience, tailors your résumé without inventing anything and tracks every application.

items.title: Campus Launch Desk
items.description: My Global Hack Week: Hacktoberfest challenges in one repo: a tested Campus Week Board mini app, one prompt benchmarked across Grok 4.7, Composer 2.5 and Gemini 4, and a two-bot Grok launch relay.

items.title: Open-source contributions
items.description: Merged fixes upstream: stabilized the queue panel hint in Breakscale's system design simulator to stop layout shifts, and fixed a failing new-service test phase in Stockroom.
